arStrings.szText:
Everything started with Lilith and Inarius, the creators of Sanctuary. They each had their own twisted plans, Lilith most of all. The world's only hope was a Wanderer who'd been fed the demon’s blood. This bond with Lilith was the key to unraveling her plans. 

Teaming up with Donan, Neyrelle, and Lorath, the Wanderer learned that Lilith wanted more than simply to empower humanity. She aimed to consume her father, Mephisto, as was being reborn in Hell. She hoped to claim his power—for Sanctuary, but even more for herself. 

Yet Mephisto had his own schemes. He sent his Herald to help the Wanderer stop Lilith. The Wanderer pursued Lilith without Mephisto as far as they could. Into the very depths of Hell. And Donan paid for it with his life. Unfortunately, in the end, they were forced to accept Mephisto's help. 

Mephisto wanted freedom. But Neyrelle imprisoned him in the soulstone, denying Lilith her prize. The Wanderer struck her down. And with her last breath, she warned of a dire future. 

"Without me," Lilith said, "you would have no victory."

Neyrelle set out to prove Lilith wrong, determined to bury the Lord of Hatred for good. But Mephisto’s corruption took hold. Luckily, the Wanderer found her and helped her to endure. Together, they found what Neyrelle had been searching for. The Tomb of Akarat—final resting place of Sanctuary’s holy prophet. 

The Wanderer defeated Mephisto's Herald, but the Lord of Hatred himself slipped through their grasp...and into a new vessel. The body of Akarat. 

Now the Lord of Hatred walks Sanctuary as a false prophet. Damnation in the guise of salvation. 

There is no time to waste. Duty demands the Wanderer face Mephisto. The fate of Sanctuary hangs in the balance.

The souls of the damned cry out, struggling in inky black waters. Mephisto's spine, a series of jagged bones, breaks the water's surface, followed by his giant, monstrous form. Souls that clung to his body rain to the shoreline of a beach, splattering the ground. "All those who touch the stone meet the same fate," Mephisto declares to a tiny, insignificant figure standing defiantly. Neyrelle. 

"No. NO! I need more time!" Neyrelle stumbles, crashing back into reality. She's in a library, countless books and tomes scattered about, while pigeons peck at the ground. She coughs blood. "I just need more time..."

She is not alone. Wearing the guise of Akarat, speaking in his voice, Mephisto taunts her. "Nothing in those scrolls will save you, Neyrelle, but I can." Neyrelle remains defiant, but Akarat sneers. "You've seen what awaits... But I can make better use of you."

"I will stop you!" Neyrelle cries, but an unseen force freezes her in place. She's back in the dream world, her feet on the edge of the cliff. Leaning back. On the cusp of plummeting. 

Mephisto's smirking head looms before her. "You think you have power here?" She falls. Down, down, down, before—

CRASH. Back in the library. Back in reality. But the lines are harder to separate. 

"I could do this for an eternity, Neyrelle," Akarat's voice continues. 

"You're right. I am a part of you," Neyrelle pants. "I was trapped in your mind. You dream. I saw the sun, blotted from the sky. And the darker it got, the brighter the rage of man burned. Hatred would reign. I was lost, but in that chaos, I found your greatest fear. And I will tell everyone." Her hand slides over parchment, the pigeons pecking at scraps on the ground.

"Oh child," Akarat says, confidence very slightly shaken. "What could I possibly fear?"

"'And the weak were made strong. The pack of lambs would feast on their shepherd,'" Neyrelle recites. 

Mephisto recognizes Rathma's prophecy, and shows rage for the first time. But Neyrelle continues, undaunted. "'Then comes a spear of Light, piercing Hatred's heart. Razed to the ground by a murdered son. And the daughter shall mold a new age from the ashes—'"

Mephisto, in a fit of fear and rage, snaps Neyrelle's neck. On her lips as she dies is a small smile. 

"You could have been so much more," Mephisto says, disappointed. He sees, wedged in his side, a knife. Neyrelle stabbed him. At first, he laughs. As if such a act could harm him. But then he gets a closer look at Neyrelle's notes. Sees a sketched figure with a blade shooting a beam of light. "Oh, what have you done?" he asks, fear slipping into his voice for the first time.

"Let them come," he says, hatred restored, as he sets the library ablaze. "Let them rise up, feeding the flames of unrest. It will not matter, for I am the light, and the way."

Meanwhile, pigeons with notes tied to their legs have been sent. Neyrelle's final message will be heard.

Over blue oceans, the Isles of Skovos come into view. The sun shines brightly as a sailing ship pulls into harbor. Much of the corruption on mainland Sanctuary has passed Skovos by, yet if you look into the distance, you can see that not all of the Skovos Isles are clean and clear. A volcano looms, lava flowing freely. 

After passing under a stone bridge, two giant statues, one of angel and one of a demon, come into view. They serve as guardians of the capital city of Skovos. Towering structures loom behind the statues, the harbor between them. It's beautiful, and imposing. Like Skovos itself.

From a high vantage point, the Wanderer watches the Amazon Queen welcome Akarat to her shores. He addresss the gathered people. "The Pools of Creation, the path to a better future, is near. And by the grace of Queen Adreona, we will reach it!" 

While the crowd cheers, Lorath walks onto the stage. He insists that Akarat is not who he claims to be. Adreona asks for proof, and Lorath offers only his word—his word as her dear friend. 

However, when Lorath opens his eyes, he no longer addresses Adreona, but Akarat himself. Akarat's voice and demeanor has shifted—no longer the kind prophet, he speaks with Mephisto's voice. Rising from the darkness is Mephisto's true, demonic head, and its tendrils lash at Lorath. In desperation, Lorath slashes Akarat's throat, blood spraying as Akarat falls.

Except, it isn't Akarat. The vision fades, revealing that Lorath has killed Adreona. The crowd is wild, but Akarat calls for no more bloodshed. He kneels behind Adreona's head and cradles it, pressing his lips to her forehead. Holy light emenates and Adreona's eyes open once more, the slash on her neck reduced to a scar.

Now convinced that Akarat is truly the prophet he claims to be, Adreona takes his hand and rises. "Let him walk free," Akarat says of Lorath, "so that all who look upon him will be reminded of what hate can do."

An Amazon warrior drags Lorath away, while Adreona and Akarat turn back to the crowd. The Wanderer leaves, worried about Lorath.

The Wanderer finds Lorath's Horadric Talisman on the ground outside of an abandoned camp. In the sky, crows from the Tree of Whispers fly overhead. Worried, the Wanderer leaves the Talisman and runs, hoping to find Lorath before the crows do. 

Lorath wanders the camp, lamenting that his efforts to stop Mephisto have been for naught. Crows circle him as he falls to his knees. "This is my fate."

Suddenly, the winds change. The crows scatter and a towering, familiar figure stands before Lorath. "Mephisto! No more damn tricks!" Lorath yells, swinging a torch at the supposed apparition. Instead, the torch is easily caught. 

True holy light bursts from the figure, revealing white, lightning-like wings. The figure extends a hand, holding the Horadric Talisman that Lorath dropped. There can be no doubt. "Tyrael." Lorath falls into the fallen angel's arms, burying his face in his chest.

"I'm sorry," Lorath says. "I've made a mess of things."

A howling gale whips across the islands of the Wanderer's mind. They stand alone, staring at a giant being, horrible bones and claws, tearing a hole in their mind. Lilith approaches, recognizing the being as Mephisto. He is linked to the Wanderer through Lilith. There is only one thing to do.

"If you are to live, you must sever the bond," Lilith says, manifesting a dagger from a single blood petal. The Wanderer, reluctantly, takes the dagger, just as Mephisto's head crashes into them.

They fall down in darkness, hearing Lilith's echoing voice. "I gave my children a world. And the strength to make it their own. And all I have to show for it...is you." Lilith reaches the Wanderer, and wraps them in her large wings. 

"Fight," Lilith commands, while her wings disintegrate from the storm Mephisto rains down. "Sever the bond!" The Wanderer, with great strength, plunges the blade into Lilith's breast. "Take your birthright and make this Sanctuary yours."

She releases the Wanderer and dies, fading away. Her bond with the Wanderer has been severed, allowing them to escape to reality.

The Wanderer finds Adreona, back turned, silhouetted against a dying campfire. Her arms are wrapped around Lorath in a lovers' embrace. Crows circle, cawing loudly. The Wanderer asks for Lorath but Adreona answers, while blood falls at her feet. 

"The man never knew when to stop," she says, breathing heavy. "Damn fool."

She turns to face the Wanderer, revealing Lorath's severed head in one hand, her blade in the other. Blood from Lorath's neck continues to fall. The crows caw louder, eager to carry their prize back to the Tree of Whispers. 

Adreona turns Lorath's face to hers, and with scorn, she declares, "A failure to the end." She tosses the head aside, turrning her full attention to the Wanderer. There is no saving her now.

Mephisto lies dying beside the Pools of Creation. "So much effort simply to return where we began," Mephisto taunts. "You, alone, just as I found you. You sacrificed everything, but changed nothing. I will be reborn in Hell, and you will be forgotten." 

But the Wanderer is undaunted. "You're not going back to Hell."

The Wanderer plunges Lilith's reforged dagger into Mephisto's heart. Screaming in pain and anger, Mephisto is pulled into the Void, where he will be locked away for untold ages. 

The cycle has been broken. The Wanderer has won.

The Wanderer raises a torch to the Tree. The white flame licks at the bark. The tree groans, nervous. And then, as if lit by accelerant, the fire catches. It snakes up the tree's side faster than the eye can move, up into the branches. The heads shriek. The crows burn.

"I brought him into this mess," the Wanderer says.

"No one brings Lorath into anything," Tyrael answers. "He made a choice. As all Horadrim do. I loved them for it." 

Lorath's head is quiet. No shouts, no screams. He closes his eyes, at peace...

The Wanderer peers into the Sightless Eye, as if peering into a well.

"Look," the Oracle says. "Do you see her?"

A vision of a hall of flesh flashes before the Wanderer's eyes, with Lilith's shadow at the far end. They peer deeper, as if falling in.

"Open her eyes."

The Wanderer approaches Lilith crouched in the center of blood petals. The Wanderer attempts to rouse her, but her body disintegrates. Yet her voice, her presence, remains. 

"Your father walks Skovos," the Wanderer says. This gets Lilith's attention. With a small smirk, she realizes why the Wanderer has sought her out.

"You need me," she says, looming over the Wanderer from behind.

In a dreamlike corner of the Mindscape, Lilith approaches an ancient doorway, overgrown with long-thorned brambles. Rathma's voice echoes from behind the doorway, an ancient and painful memory.

She reaches, tenderly, for the door, pulling from it a memory of a strange dagger. "I gave him a weapon," Lilith says. "He rejected it." As she speaks, the dagger she holds shatters to three pieces. 

"But, if it can be restored, then this...this is what will end my father's reign." The pieces of the dagger vanish back into the memory, leaving Lilith alone with the Wanderer once more.

In a tent, while she leans over a table of maps and plans, Lorath pleads with Adreona to reconsider her support of Akarat. "I know Akarat's tricks. He is death."

He approaches her from behind, slowly, cautiously. Their hands meet, and Lorath, softly, pleads. "I let him use me. I’m sorry."

But his touch is a step too far. Adreona grabs him by the throat and raises him off his feet, choking him, her face full of rage. "You call Akarat death?" she says. "Only one has ever left me bleeding out on the floor."

Lorath turns blue, his eyes rolling in his head. Adreona continues, "You are a failed guardian. Of your land, your people, your legacy. I won't be."

Tears well in Lorath's eyes, and she throws him to the floor. Without giving him a second glance, she storms out of the tent, leaving one parting message, "Stay on Athulua and condemn yourself, but I will suffer sparing you no longer."

Adreona is gone. Only the Queen remains.

Tyrael approaches the writhing mass blocking the entrance to the Pools of Creation. Instructing the Wanderer to move quickly, he grips El'druin, his sword, and leaps at the entrance. The barrier’s faces release unearthly screams as El'druin stabs into its center.

Angelic light bursts from Tyrael's sword, holding the barrier open. His grip on El'druin shakes but holds firm. "This is your birthplace!" Tyrael shouts. "Take it back!" 

The Wanderer approaches the opening in the barrier, knowing that they haven't a moment to waste.

The Wanderer approaches Akarat, as he leads another follower into the Pools of Creation. The Wanderer calls out, "Mephisto! That's enough."

Akarat stops, turning to the Wanderer. Reality warps around them, and Akarat's voice transforms into Mephisto's. The demon taunts the Wanderer, until they can take no more, and they stab Akarat in the stomach with Lilith's blade.

They return to reality, with the crowd looking in horror as Akarat, stabbed, stumbles toward the Pools of Creation. He recognizes the blade, and removes it from his body, his disguise faltering. He tumbles into the waters, and from his body, the waters turn back with corruption.

The pieces of Lilith's blade have been gathered, and all that remains is to assemble it with the Horadric Cube. Lorath and Tyrael work in sync, reminiscing about the past and trading light jabs.

After Lorath helps Tyrael complete a pivotal part of the process, Tyrael remembers when he and Lorath first met. Back then, Lorath had asked Tyrael how it felt to become mortal. Tyrael muses, "You were compassionate. 
You showed me how to be human. That’s how I knew the Order was in good hands, when I left. And it still is. Look. We’ve shaped the blade that will banish a Prime Evil."

Lilith's blade is indeed complete. They take a moment to admire their work, but the moment is short-lived. The Wanderer gets painful visions of their mindscape, corrupted by Mephisto. They collapse, Tyrael and Lorath coming to their aid.

In weary, aching silence, the Wanderer falls to their knees beside Lorath's body. Tyrael walks heavily to join them, head bowed in grief. "Your duty is done," Tyrael says, a prayer for Lorath.

The Wanderer's rage gets the better of them. "'Duty.'... He gave everything he had for it, and this? This is his reward? Betrayed and murdered! Damned to eternity on the Tree of Whispers! And all the while...Mephisto laughs, as we fall."

Tyrael approaches the Wanderer, and offers Lilith's blade to them. "Lorath would tell us to leave him here. To ride out with your Mother's weapon, and drive it into Mephisto's heart. To save as many souls as we can."

The Wanderer somberly takes the blade—they know Tyrael is right. Recalling Lorath's words, they say, "The dead deserve nothing...while the living are in danger."

Tyrael nods. "So he said. But we will bury him at least."

Sometime later, the Wanderer comes across a Lilith statue, enveloped in bright sunlight. Red petals, from a tree growing around the statue, fall at Lilith's feet. The Wanderer looks into Lilith's stone eyes. 

"She created this Sanctuary, even though she knew that all of it could be swept away at any moment," Tyrael muses from afar.

The Wanderer continues on their way, out of Lilith's shadow.

"But she believed someone would choose to walk in her footsteps—someone would stand in defiance of fate itself and protect this fragile world."

The Wanderer stands at the side of a ship, sailing through the sea. They drop a few red petals into the water--petals that they had gathered from the statue. Then they look ahead, to their destination, Temis, radiant and bright. A new dawn, a new day, a new era.

"You could call it madness," Tyrael concludes. "I call it hope."

LATER--

There's a soft breeze in the air. 
A blood petal rests in the wanderer's palm. It lingers for just a moment... before disintegrating into the wind. They push themselves up onto their elbows and sweep their eyes across the horizon. 

Their mindscape is empty. Serene. And so quiet.
The wanderer stands. They are alive. And alone.
